main_body: Tree with a rounded leaf canopy (several overlapping clumps) on a single brown trunk with a flared root base
top_band: Canopy: the topmost clump at x=29 shows light green (L~110) at rows 1-2, then mid greens down to a dark underside; no flat horizontal top surface, as is normal for a tree crown
evidence: Organic tree: each canopy lobe is lit on top (light greens) and shaded underneath, with dark undersides that separate the lobes and the trunk, so it reads as a volumetric 3/4 form and not as a flat elevation. The trunk is a vertical shaft with a flared base, normal for a tree. No receding side faces and no top-down slab. The organic kind does not require a flat horizontal surface.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 15 distinct colours and a median of 8 colours per tile, against about 108 per tile and 427-567 colours for the references. The canopy has about 4 green steps with scattered highlight dots, but the clumps are smooth and blobby and lack the per-leaf clustering of the references. The trunk is a brown ramp with vertical grain, but it is simple. Outlines are near-black/very dark green and neutral on 20% of edge pixels, so they are mixed and lean toward the sticker look. Clearly thinner than the references in colour count and detail.
